title: Per-parameter efficiency, edge-scale prototype
label: edge-scale prototype comparison, not performance parity with 27B-class MPU

methodology.basis: Measured synthesis of the shipped bitstream's design and of the full ternary-MAC datapath probe (yosys synth_xilinx -family xc7 -nodsp -nosrl -flatten).
methodology.params_definition: The ternary MAC datapath implements one 8-bit-activation x ternary-weight product stage. Parameter count is reported for the DEMONSTRATED workload only: the weights that would be resident in the fabric for a 1-2M-parameter tiny ternary transformer block are counted at 2 bits each (ternary {-1,0,+1} in 2-bit code).
methodology.params_scope: 1-2M parameter tiny ternary transformer block, per LL1_RESOURCE_BUDGET.md. This is NOT a 27B model and the table is NOT a parity benchmark.
methodology.caveat: The token/s and J/token columns are the values measured on the demonstrated MAC+ring-oscillator bitstream, not on a 1-2M-parameter transformer. The per-parameter normalisation therefore says how much headroom the measured primitive leaves, not what a full 1-2M block would achieve.

ternary_mac_datapath_probe.description: full ternary MAC with all 32 accumulator bits observed

measured_throughput_and_energy.tokens_per_sec_status: MEASURED (5 cycle-1 runs / 0.875 s total, CV 0.46%)

rows.params_note: one 8-bit-activation ternary-weight stage; 64 ternary weights at 2 bits = 128 bits = 0.000064 M params

rows.workload: tiny ternary transformer block, 1M params (target scope)
rows.note: NOT MEASURED. 1M ternary weights at 2 bits = 250 kB. The MAC probe uses 18 LCs, so 1M weights would need roughly 1M/64 x 18 = 281k LCs if each weight consumed a full MAC stage - more than twice the XC7A200T fabric. The weights must be packed in BRAM and streamed, which changes the design entirely. Recorded as an open feasibility question, not a claim.

rows.workload: tiny ternary transformer block, 2M params (target scope)
rows.note: NOT MEASURED. Same open feasibility question as the 1M row.

explicit_non_claims: This is NOT a comparison against a 27B-class MPU.
The 1M and 2M rows are NOT measurements; they are scope markers with an open feasibility question.
No claim of tokens/sec at 1-2M scale, no claim of J/token at 1-2M scale.
The only measured throughput belongs to the demonstrated MAC primitive.
Literature baselines (TeLLMe 0.7B @ 9.51 tok/s / 7 W on Kria KV260) are context only, not a comparison target, because they are a different model class and a different measurement contract.
